implementation_notes: `Sequence.filter(_:)` is a standard-library protocol extension: the closure is the criterion and the result is an Array of the elements that satisfy it, so the loop body never sees rejects; `.lazy.filter` keeps the pipeline lazy for long feeds and an AsyncSequence filters inside a `for await` loop. The newer Foundation overload takes a `Predicate<Element>` value, which - unlike a closure - can be built from a string expression or decoded, making it the closest stdlib analogue to a configured criterion (iOS 17 / macOS 14 and later). A filter type is justified only when the criterion must be an injected, named component.
pitfalls: filter on a Sequence is eager and returns `[Element]`: on long or unbounded feeds use `.lazy.filter` (or an AsyncSequence) or the whole feed is copied.
A non-Collection sequence may consume itself when iterated, so filtering the same sequence twice can silently produce nothing the second time.
A closure predicate cannot be serialised or decoded; configuration-driven criteria need the Predicate overload or an explicit criterion type.

variants.name: Reactive pipeline filter (Combine)
variants.implementation_notes: In a Combine pipeline the filter is an operator: `publisher.filter { ... }` republishes only the elements the closure accepts and drops the rest before any subscriber sees them, so the criterion lives inside the declarative pipeline instead of in a component. Use it when messages already flow as publishers (URLSession, notifications, KVO); the trade-off is that drops are invisible, so count rejections inside the closure when the accepted rate matters. Combine is Apple-platform only (iOS 13 / macOS 10.15 and later).
pitfalls: Dropped values are invisible: a filter that rejects everything leaves a live-looking pipeline that never fires, so count rejections inside the closure.
Sink closures capture strongly and retaining self or an object graph creates reference cycles unless `[weak self]` is used.
A publisher filter can only shrink the stream; criteria that must observe every value (audit, metrics) belong before the filter or on a duplicated pipeline.
